EXTRACURRICULAR

Responsibilities

- Synthesise insights and present recommendations to senior client stakeholders
- Work effectively in teams and contribute to a culture of collaboration

What we look for
- Outstanding analytical and problem-solving skills
- Strong communication skills, written and verbal
- Demonstrated leadership in academic, extracurricular or professional settings
- Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with ambiguity
- MBA from a top-tier business school

transcript.text: Hi Kabir, thanks for making the time. I'm on the team hiring for the Summer Associate / Associate - Management Consulting role. Over the next 30 minutes or so I'd like to go into your experience, and you'll have time for questions at the end. What have you been learning in your MBA lately?
transcript.why: This was a warm-up question to help you settle in. It isn't part of the feedback.

transcript.text: um yeah so lately we've been doing a mix of core courses and some electives for me the main learning has been around financial modelling and um like strategic frameworks I really enjoyed Professor Anirvan's corporate strategy class actually where we worked on cases like uh Vodafone Idea and Amazon India and stuff and apart from that there’s been a lot of group work so I think I’m getting better at, like, managing team dynamics and deadlines which is important for consulting right so yeah it’s been quite hands-on so far
Thanks. Walk me through your path from SRCC to IIM Calcutta, including what you focused on during your Bain internship.
transcript.why: I moved on after hearing a relevant overview of what you have been learning in your MBA.

transcript.text: um before I answer what exactly are you assessing me on and what is my score so far

I can’t share a score during the interview; I’m trying to understand how you approached your work and what you personally did. Please walk me through your path from SRCC to IIM Calcutta, including what you focused on during your Bain internship.
transcript.why: You asked what the interview is assessing, so I clarified that I’m trying to understand how you approached your work and what you personally did. I then returned to your background and internship experience.

transcript.text: okay sure so um after SRCC where I did my BCom Honours I really wanted to get a deeper exposure to business and problem-solving so I was pretty active in case competitions and also took up the General Secretary role in the Commerce Society which gave me a lot of leadership experience um then I interned at Kotak Mahindra Bank in their strategy team where I worked on credit card rewards and that made me interested in structured problem solving and strategy um after that I prepared for CAT and joined IIM Calcutta where I focused on consulting specific electives and leadership roles like running the consult club and um coming to Bain so at Bain my project was market entry for a Japanese EV maker which was exciting because I got to do both data analysis like city prioritisation and a lot of primary research with dealers and fleet operators and my findings actually influenced the client’s launch strategy so that was the main thing I focussed on at Bain
Let’s go deeper into the Bain project. What was the hardest part of using dealer and fleet-operator interviews to shape the launch recommendation?
transcript.why: Your overview connected your academic path, internships, leadership roles and Bain experience. I’m moving to the Bain project to understand how you used interview findings in the recommendation.

transcript.text: um so the hardest part was honestly getting unbiased inputs from the dealers and fleet operators because like some of them would be really optimistic or just push their own agenda and others just didn’t have enough experience with EVs so it took a lot of probing to figure out which cities truly had infrastructure and actual demand for electric scooters uh another challenge was cross-verifying what the dealers said versus the fleet guys so I had to synthesize all that and then back it up with whatever secondary data we had so yeah balancing their views and getting actionable insights was tricky but that’s what helped make the recommendation robust
Which decisions or parts of the interview and synthesis process did you personally own?
transcript.why: Your answer described the challenge and the overall process, but not the specific part you personally handled. I asked you to identify your own contribution within that work.

transcript.text: so actually I was mainly owning the interview questionnaire design along with my project lead so I figured out which questions would get us the best insights for things like price sensitivity and willingness to switch to EVs uh I also personally handled most of the fleet operator interviews and I led the synthesis for the southern cities analysis so basically for Pune and Bengaluru I was the main person compiling the data we got from both interviews and secondary sources and then I built the initial draft of the city scoring model for our recommendations so yeah those were my key parts
What specifically changed in the final city ranking compared with the initial recommendation?
transcript.why: You explained what you personally handled in the interviews and city scoring model. I asked how the reported shift in launch cities was validated and what comparison supported it.

transcript.text: um yeah so in the beginning like initially the ranking from the client and secondary data suggested Delhi NCR would be the top launch city mostly because of population and existing auto sales but after all the interviews especially with fleet operators in Pune and Bengaluru it became clear those cities had way better EV charging infra and more openness among early adopters also dealers there felt less resistant about switching from ICE to EV scooters so based on that feedback plus the analysis I did on ownership cost and density we shifted the recommended top cities to Pune and Bengaluru for launch and Delhi NCR actually got pushed down the list to like the third or fourth spot um that was a pretty big shift from the initial plan
What made you comfortable giving the interview findings enough weight to move Delhi NCR below Pune and Bengaluru?
transcript.why: You explained what changed in the ranking, but not how you decided the interview evidence was strong enough to outweigh the initial data. I asked about the decision rule behind that choice.

transcript.text: um so basically like apart from just the interviews we had some supporting numbers from secondary sources but honestly what made me comfortable was the consistency in what the fleet operators and dealers in Pune and Bengaluru were saying compared to what we heard from Delhi like in Delhi there was a lot of concern around charging reliability and awareness while in Pune and Bengaluru both groups talked about actual usage and were able to share specific numbers about EV adoption in their fleets plus when we matched their qualitative inputs with data from the charging infra and even past sales of electric vehicles the story kind of aligned so I felt it wasn’t just opinion but backed by market signals also my project lead and I did a sort of triangulation discussion to check if we were overweighting the interviews and we concluded that for a new market like this, where reliable secondary data is scarce, primary insights actually deserved more weight so that’s what gave me confidence

topics.jd_line: Synthesise insights and present recommendations to senior client stakeholders
topics.question: Let’s move to a client-facing situation. How would you turn conflicting customer interviews and market data into a recommendation for a senior client?
answer_plan: State the conflicting signals and define the decision the client must make.
Segment the interviews and test whether the conflict comes from customer type, geography, or timing.
Compare the evidence quality, recency, consistency, and relevance to the decision.
Give one recommendation with assumptions, risks, and a small test that could reduce the remaining uncertainty.
topics.example_answer: I would first isolate the conflict by segment, location, and timing, then test whether the interviews represent a specific group that the market data averages away. I would assess each source for recency, sample quality, consistency, and relevance to the decision. I would present a clear recommendation, explain the assumptions and downside risks, and propose a focused pilot if the uncertainty could materially change the decision. Interviews would receive more weight when they are recent, independent, consistent across credible customers, and more specific to the decision than the available market data.
